content: Dihydroartemisinin (DHA) is the active metabolite of artemether. The metabolism of artemether is primarily catalyzed by the cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP3A4, with lesser contributions from CYP2B6, CYP2C9, and CYP2C19. In vitro studies conducted at therapeutic concentrations of artemether demonstrated no significant inhibition of the metabolic activities of CYP1A2, CYP2A6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP2E1, CYP3A4/5, or CYP4A9/11. Similarly, in vitro studies with artemether, DHA, and lumefantrine at therapeutic concentrations showed no significant induction of the metabolic activities of CYP1A1, CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP3A4, or CYP3A5. During repeated administration of artemether and lumefantrine tablets, systemic exposure to artemether decreased significantly, while DHA concentrations increased, though not to a statistically significant degree, after six doses administered over three days. This observation suggests the induction of enzymes responsible for artemether metabolism. In human liver microsomes and recombinant CYP450 enzymes, lumefantrine is metabolized primarily by CYP3A4 into desbutyl-lumefantrine. However, systemic exposure to desbutyl-lumefantrine is less than 1% of the exposure to the parent compound. In vitro, lumefantrine significantly inhibits CYP2D6 activity at therapeutic plasma concentrations. Co-administration of artemether and lumefantrine tablets with CYP2D6 substrates may lead to increased plasma concentrations of the CYP2D6 substrate, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. Artemether and DHA are cleared from plasma with an elimination half-life of approximately two hours. Lumefantrine, on the other hand, is eliminated more slowly, with an elimination half-life of 3 to 6 days in healthy volunteers and patients with falciparum malaria. Demographic factors such as sex and weight do not appear to have clinically relevant effects on the pharmacokinetics of artemether and lumefantrine. Artemether and lumefantrine are active against the erythrocytic stages of Plasmodium falciparum. Strains of P. falciparum with moderate decreases in susceptibility to artemether or lumefantrine alone can be selected in vitro or in vivo, but such resistance is not maintained in the case of artemether. The clinical relevance of this phenomenon remains unknown. Carcinogenicity studies have not been conducted, and no evidence of mutagenicity was detected in various tests, including the Salmonella and Escherichia/mammalian-microsome mutagenicity test, the gene mutation test with Chinese hamster cells, the cytogenetic test on Chinese hamster cells in vitro, and the rat micronucleus test in vivo. Neonatal rats (7–21 days old) were found to be more sensitive to the toxic effects of artemether than older juvenile rats or adults. Mortality and severe clinical signs were observed in neonatal rats at doses that were well tolerated in pups older than 22 days. The efficacy of artemether and lumefantrine tablets for the treatment of acute, uncomplicated malaria caused by P. falciparum was evaluated in eight clinical studies involving HIV-negative patients. Uncomplicated malaria was defined as symptomatic P. falciparum malaria without signs or symptoms of severe malaria or evidence of vital organ dysfunction. These studies included partially immune and non-immune adults and children (weighing ≥5 kg) with uncomplicated malaria in regions such as China, Thailand, sub-Saharan Africa, Europe, and South America. Patients with severe malaria or significant cardiac, renal, or hepatic impairment were excluded. The studies included two trials assessing the efficacy of the individual components of the regimen, a study comparing a 4-dose versus a 6-dose regimen, and five additional studies evaluating the 6-dose regimen. Artemether and lumefantrine tablets were administered at 0, 8, 24, and 48 hours in the 4-dose regimen, and at 0, 8, 24, 36, 48, and 60 hours in the 6-dose regimen. The modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population included all patients with confirmed malaria diagnoses who received at least one dose of the study drug. Evaluated patients were those who had parasitological assessments on days 7 and 28 or experienced treatment failure by day 28. Two randomized, double-blind, comparative, single-center studies conducted in China assessed the efficacy of artemether and lumefantrine tablets (4 doses of 4 tablets containing 20 mg artemether/120 mg lumefantrine) compared to each component administered alone.
